verdicts.citation: SPEC.md 7.6 'Lab timings' bullet: 'Tools reserve their box size in the HTML so that hydration does not shift the page.' This sentence is a direct requirement, unqualified and not limited to the lab load. It supports the finding's expected.
verdicts.evidence: I read everything at gate commit b9b8504, in a detached worktree that is still clean. SPEC 7.6 has the heading [D]. The reserved-box sentence has no qualifier ('may', 'where the layout allows') and does not depend on how the lab is measured. SPEC 4 T10 'Presets' says the data files are 'fetched' by the tool. Neither it nor 4.0 'Works before and without JavaScript' / 7.4 allows hydrated markup that differs from the server markup while the fetch runs. T10 and M7 are phase 4 (SPEC 4 heading 'T10. Geometry Studio (phase 4)'; 9.1 row 4), so they are inside gate G4. Recorded decisions read: (1) decisions/P4-A3.md, 'the snapshot without JavaScript, and the SVG of the view'. It reserves only the figure box ('aspect-ratio: 1 ... so the canvas replaces the snapshot without shift once the configured orbit is complete') and says 'after any change' the canvas shows what is known. It says nothing about the output lines during hydration. (2) decisions/RT-FIX-P3-nojs-phase4.md, P4-MERGE-03. It makes the server markup the state 'as the browser does' ('data-out="source" is shown whenever the orbit is complete, before hydration as after'). The finding's observed (source, shared and drawn lines emptied at hydration) goes against what that record intends. The source matches the location: T10GeometryStudio.svelte initialOrbit returns 'ready' from ssr.data at build time and { kind: 'pending' } in the browser. The oracle has nothing to say about layout. Records searched with no match: DECISIONS.md, every decisions/*.md, the known-and-decided list in P4-LENS-INSTRUCTIONS.md, gate-G4.md (report commit 4e3e839, which names b9b8504 as the gate commit), and the round 1 confirmed and deferred JSON. None accepts a transient pending state that empties lines. Note: the CLS figures were taken at a scrolled reading position, which is not the lab's load at the top. The finding does not depend on them, because the reserved-box sentence applies to every hydration, including client:visible islands.
verdicts.reason: not refuted: R1, no sentence allows hydration to change a tool's markup or height (7.6's reserved-box sentence is unqualified); R2, the finding quotes 7.6 correctly and a 24 px shrink and regrow at hydration is a shift of the page; R3, T10 and M7 are phase 4 and the gate is G4; R4, no oracle quantity is involved; R5, 7.6 is [D], but P4-A3 reserves only the figure box and RT-FIX-P3-nojs-phase4 intends the server markup to equal the hydrated default, so a departure from the [D] text is not covered; R6, no record of this cause in gate-G4.md, the round 1 files or the merge reports on disk. Major matches the rubric: a stated behaviour, the reserved box, is wrong.

verdicts.citation: SPEC.md 7.6 'Lab timings' bullet: 'Tools reserve their box size in the HTML so that hydration does not shift the page.' SPEC 4.0 'Predict' [D]: 'Without JavaScript the question is followed by a <details> element holding the answer and the reveal.' The first supports the finding's expected. The second sets the form for readers without JavaScript and allows no change of size at hydration.
verdicts.evidence: I read everything at b9b8504. In T10GeometryStudio.svelte, Predict.svelte is imported in an $effect: 'until it arrives the static question and its <details> stand'. decisions/P4-A3.md, 'the size of /tools/geometry/', records this lazy load for the 90 kB route limit of 7.6 and says the static form is 'the same no-JavaScript form as Predict's'. The same fragment's '[D] items' entry claims '7.6 [D] (... reserved box)' was followed. The finding reports the box growing from 128 to 278 px at hydration, so the recorded choice departs from the [D] text it relies on. RT-VERIFY 5.4: 'R5 holds for a choice within the text, never for a departure from it.' DECISIONS.md line 2877 (T10_PROP_ONLY_OUTS) describes Predict's server markup before Predict arrives. It does not accept a shift. SPEC 4.0 'Predict' prescribes the form without JavaScript. It does not say that a page with JavaScript may grow when the interactive form replaces it. M7 and T10 are phase 4, so inside G4. The lens file's own rule (RT-07 section 6) keeps the reserved-box rule 'reportable from phase 0'. No record in gate-G4.md, the round 1 files (the deferred P4-MERGE-02 is a different cause: the answer missing without JavaScript) or the merge logs on disk. Note: the CLS figures (0.1080 with fonts blocked, growth shift alone 0.0834) were taken at a scrolled reading position, not in the lab's load at the top. The finding rests on the reserved-box sentence, which is independent of that.
verdicts.reason: not refuted: R1, 4.0 'Predict' fixes the form without JavaScript but no sentence allows the island to grow at hydration; R2, the finding reads the reserved-box sentence correctly; R3, phase 4 at gate G4; R4, the oracle is not involved; R5, P4-A3's lazy-Predict record is a size choice that departs from the reserved-box text it claims to follow, so it is not covered; R6, no record of this cause. Major matches the rubric: a stated behaviour is wrong.

verdicts.citation: SPEC.md 7.6 'Lab timings' [D]: 'on the built site with a mobile profile (360 by 800 pixels, processor slowed four times): ... Total Blocking Time at most 200 ms, Cumulative Layout Shift at most 0.1 ... The intended tool is Lighthouse CI'. SPEC 9.1 G4: 'lab timings on M6 and M7'. The TBT half of the finding stands on these. The CLS half does not, because 7.6's CLS line is a lab timing and the recorded lab method (decisions/P3-A7.md) is a Lighthouse navigation of the route, not a reload at a restored scroll position.
verdicts.evidence: Read at b9b8504. CLS half: 7.6 puts CLS among the three 'Lab timings' and names Lighthouse CI as the tool. It separates lab numbers from field data ('Interaction to Next Paint, which only field data can measure, is checked by hand'). decisions/P3-A7.md 'the lab tool is Lighthouse CI (Branch A)' and 'the three numbers and the end of the measurement' record that CLS is 'the numericValue of Lighthouse's audits ... cumulative-layout-shift' of a run on the route. That is a fresh navigation at the top. gate-G4.md section 8 (report commit 4e3e839) measured CLS 0.0003 on M6 and 0.0000 on M7, and the finding agrees ('the lab run does not see the shift'; M7 y=0 0.0770). The reproducer (522fae9:redteam/redteam-RT-07-font-swap-shift.mjs, read as text) loads the page, scrolls with window.scrollTo, then reloads. That scenario is outside the measurement 7.6 and P3-A7 define. The reserved-box sentence covers hydration, not font loading. font-display:block is in KaTeX 0.16.47's own stylesheet, which 7.2 item 2 and CLAUDE.md require to be shipped from the installed version (P0-A3: 'the stylesheet and fonts are copied from that package'). No KaTeX decision in P0-A3, P1-A2 or P0-A5 addresses preloading. TBT half: DECISIONS.md 'P3-X1: other load work looked at (c)' records 'no repeated layout from late fonts was large in the traces, so no preload was added'. That was measured on M0 to M3 before M6 and M7 existed. MERGE P3 stage 3.3 kept the render hint and named the first tool's hydration as what remains. The owner's acceptance ('OWNER: gate G3's lab item accepted as machine-bound') covers G3 on M0 to M5 only. gate-G4.md is RED on M7's TBT (381.3 ms), puts it down to 'likely hydration' and sends it to this round. The known-and-decided list says 'M7's number ... is' still open. The cause the finding names (font relayout after FCP adding about 120 ms on M7) is therefore not recorded or accepted. A builder's no-preload record cannot cover a TBT over the 200 ms of the [D] text.
verdicts.reason: not refuted: the cause, late KaTeX fonts relaid out after FCP, stands for M7's Total Blocking Time over 200 ms at G4, which no record accepts (owner's acceptance limited to G3 M0 to M5; gate-G4 sends M7 to this round; P3-X1's no-preload record predates M7 and cannot cover a departure from 7.6). Part note: the CLS half (0.30 to 0.33 on a reload at a restored scroll position) is not a violation of 7.6, because 7.6's CLS line is a lab timing, recorded by P3-A7 as Lighthouse's navigation of the route, where M6 and M7 measure 0.0003 and 0.0000 (R2 and R5 hold for that half only). R1 no permitting clause for TBT; R3 M7 is phase 4; R4 not an oracle quantity; R6 gate-G4 records the symptom with a different presumed cause. Major matches the rubric for the TBT half: a stated threshold is exceeded at a gate that requires it.

verdicts.citation: R1: SPEC.md 7.6 'Main-thread work': 'No engine call on the main thread may become a long task (50 ms) on that phone.' The finding's own numbers show this bound respected. R2: the SPEC.md 7.6 table states 'the gzip size of all JavaScript the route fetches' and the tool route consists of 'the tool's own code with the engine functions only it uses'. t02/presets.ts and t08/presets.ts are T2's and T8's own modules, on T2's and T8's own pages. R5: DECISIONS.md '2026-10-10 P1-A6: properties and presets': 'Captions take their numbers from the engine at module load (12, 6, 6, 243, 6), never typed.'
verdicts.evidence: Read at b9b8504. The finding's observed: TRIANGLE_GROWTH 30.6 to 47.1 ms inclusive at 4x (classify 13 to 41 ms; this inclusive figure covers several engine calls), rootCount 16.6 ms, the triangle search 0.61 ms warm in Node. The finding's coverage lists the T8 calls on A3 among calls that do not reach 25 ms. No single engine call reaches the 50 ms of 7.6, even at 4x slowdown on a container the owner recorded as about 2.3 times slower than the reference processor (DECISIONS.md 'OWNER: gate G3's lab item'). The 7.6 table limits and describes the bytes a route fetches. It says nothing about when a tool's own code runs. On /tools/garden/, M1, M3, M4 and M6 (T2) and /tools/weyl/ and M5 (T8), the preset modules are the tool's own code, and roots, positiveRoots, orbitGraph, boardFromName and the classify called through resolveBoard, plus weylOrder, legalLayers, countCompleteGames and commutationClassSize, are engine functions those tools use. The routes are within their limits (finding's coverage). T2's module-load captions are logged: P1-A6 (quoted above), with MERGE P1 accepting 'preset options in t02/presets.ts'. COMMON.md 4.4 forbids 'a golden value typed into source'. Round 1's P3-RT-07-04 (round1-confirmed-B.json) claimed 'computing captions of tools that are not on the page' through the eager registry. decisions/RT-FIX-P3-perf-b.md removed that cross-tool path, and the finding's own coverage says that fix holds. Own presets on the tool's own pages are outside that claim. The lens's own attack 22 treats engine calls under 25 ms on a desktop as not even a note. No sentence of 7.6 or 4.0 forbids a tool's own module from calling the engine when it loads.
verdicts.reason: 7.6 states a 50 ms bound per main-thread engine call, which the finding's own measurements show is respected (R1). The 7.6 table governs bytes and composition, and these preset modules and the engine functions they call are T2's and T8's own on their own pages (R2). P1-A6 records that T2's captions take their numbers from the engine at module load (R5). Round 1's P3-RT-07-04 concerned other tools' presets on every route, and the RT-FIX-P3-perf-b fix that removed that cause holds.

verdicts.citation: SPEC.md 7.6 table: '/tools/<id>': 'shell, shared code, and the tool's own code with the engine functions only it uses'; 'any lesson page': 'shell, shared code, the first tool of the page, and any other tool in view'. decisions/RT-FIX-P3-perf-b.md, 'the browser never loads the tool registry (P3-RT-07-04)'. Both support the finding's expected.
verdicts.evidence: Read at b9b8504. The finding's expected matches site/src/tools/offered.ts: its header says it imports 'only the small lists the registry entries themselves read, never an entry, a preset module or an engine function', and its lines 11 and 12 import T10_BOARDS from t10/config and T11_BOARDS from t11/config. t10/config.ts exports T10_PRESETS (eight presets with board, rings, projection and caption), the eight *_CAPTION strings and T10_OUTS. t11/config.ts exports T11_PRESETS, CONSTRUCTION and the FOLD and AVERAGE captions. So both are preset-holding modules. The RT-FIX-P3-perf-b record does name t10/config and t11/config, but as 'the light board lists'. Its stated reason was that the registry 'put every tool's registry entry and presets ... into the ToolFrame chunk of every tool route and lesson'. T10's preset table and captions in the ToolFrame chunk on routes without T10 depart from that record's own rule, so the record does not cover them (R5 holds only for a choice within the text). In the 7.6 table, another tool's preset captions on /tools/board/ or M0 are not the shell, not the shared code 7.6 names (Svelte runtime, engine core, board components) and not that route's tool. All routes stay within their limits. The lens file's section 6 excludes only the 45 kB and 30 kB sub-figures when the limit holds, not the composition. Attack 12 counts unused code within the limit as minor. T10 and T11 are phase 4, at gate G4. No record in gate-G4.md, the known-and-decided list, or the round 1 files: round 1's P3-RT-07-04 fix is the source of this import.
verdicts.reason: not refuted: R1, the 7.6 table's composition columns do not allow another tool's presets and captions in the chunk every route fetches, and the limits holding only keeps this minor; R2, the finding reads the table and the RT-FIX-P3-perf-b rule ('never ... a preset module') correctly; R3, T10 and T11 are phase 4 at G4; R4, the oracle is not involved; R5, RT-FIX-P3-perf-b names t10/config and t11/config only as 'light board lists', and the build departs from that record's own rule; R6, no record. Minor matches the rubric: unused bytes within the limit.
